lesson_title: One Logbook, One Wallet, One Pipe: Physics Exam Essentials
hook_text: A 3 kg ball and a 30 kg ball dropped from 10 m land at EXACTLY the same speed. One cancelled letter explains the whole thing.
clip_script: Set a half m v squared equal to m g h and the mass cancels: v squared equals 2 g h. The landing speed of a freely falling object does not depend on its mass — a 3-kilogram ball and a 30-kilogram ball from 10 metres both arrive at 14 metres per second. Heavier means more energy, but also more energy needed for the same speed, and the two effects cancel exactly.
visual_style: Two balls of wildly different sizes falling side by side in perfect sync; the equation a half m v squared equals m g h on screen with both m symbols dissolving; a landing freeze-frame stamped 14 metres per second on each ball.
mood: Myth-busting swagger — the intuition everyone has, disproved by one line of algebra.
pacing: Quick setup of the heavier-falls-faster instinct, the cancellation beat in slow motion, synchronised landing payoff.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision lesson and run the whole year's physics through three pictures that never fail.
